name: Naturalist Watercolour Plate
description: A finished nineteenth-century naturalist plate: precise watercolour and gouache over fine ink detail on aged paper, specimen clarity in a soft muted earth and sea-green palette, painted edge to edge.
style_bible: A finished nineteenth-century natural-history plate, reproduced from a hand-painted original on aged paper. Medium and surface: precise watercolour and gouache laid over a fine ink drawing. The ink establishes structure and small detail — veins, scales, fibres, joints, the exact edge of a shell — and is drawn finely and deliberately, never as a heavy contour; the paint then builds form in controlled layers that move from translucent in the lights to opaque in the solids. Nothing is loose: there is no wet-in-wet accident, no granulation left as a gesture, and no uncovered sketch. Palette: soft muted earths and sea-greens — ochre, olive, umber, slate green, bone — at low saturation and in harmonious values, with a small saturated note allowed only where the subject itself would show one. Lighting: even, diffuse and observational, describing form with subtle modelled washes rather than with a dramatic key; the light exists to make the specimen legible, not to make a picture. Composition: the subject is painted as a finished plate that fills the frame edge to edge. There is no border, no margin and no ring of blank paper around the subject; the ground behind it is a soft neutral within the same palette, painted rather than left bare. Aged paper: a light even tone and a faint fibrous texture are welcome. Absolutely no labels, plate numbers, captions, handwriting, arrows, scale bars or signatures anywhere in the frame. Content-independent: no fixed species, era, institution or copied plate.
